original_declarations.obj: why an agent needs a model of how to build the thing, not just a picture of it
original_declarations.statement: After this section, the reader can explain why an agent, like a 3D printer, needs the detailed build instructions and not merely a picture of the desired result.
original_declarations.anchor: point: modeling-and-alignment-supply-the-instruction-package (The Printer, 'The Engineering Object' — intent is not fabrication instructions; a photograph does not specify the build).

original_declarations.obj: the posture that when an agent produces the wrong thing, the first suspect is the instructions
original_declarations.statement: After this section, the reader can adopt the posture that an agent is a printer, not a stapler — so when it produces the wrong thing, the first suspect is the instructions, and the models can build anything one can explain.
Building with an agent is running a printer, not a coder: suspect the instructions before the agent's capability.
original_declarations.contradicted_by: Treating a bad output as a fixed capability ceiling by reflex, without first examining the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment.
original_declarations.anchor: Preface through-line + 1.1 the-printer / whose-fault-is-it: the agent is a printer; a bad output is first evidence about the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment, not by reflex a fixed capability ceiling.
